newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Anderton lodges complaint against Treasurer.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Anderton lodges complaint against Treasurer.

text.p: Left-wing Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Thursday he had lodged a breach of privileges complaint against New Zealand Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters over an incident in parliament on Wednesday.

Anderton alleges Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters pushed and argued with National backbencher John Banks over Banks' stance on a key piece of government legislation postponing tax cuts.
His complaint was lodged with parliament's speaker.
Anderton also said Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare had physically prevented Radio New Zealand journalist Stephen Parker from trying to record the incident.

Free market Act New Zealand Party leader Richard Prebble, who said he observed the later part of the incident, has also lodged a complaint about Peters, Henare and Associate Education Minister Brian Donnelly.
Peters denies manhandling Banks but apologised to him on Thursday over the dispute, and Henare has apologised to Parker.
Banks said he accepted the apology and would not pursue a complaint of his own.
Peters' New Zealand First formed a coalition government with National in December, which controls 61 seats in the 120-member parliament.

Anderton told a news conference: "The key issue is not Mr Peters has apologised to Mr Banks or Mr Henare has apologised to Mr Parker...the issue is the behaviour which was both a contempt of parliament and a breach of the privileges of parliament."
Anderton, who witnessed the fracas, said he expected the Speaker to report on whether the matter would be referred to parliament's privileges committee on Tuesday.
"It was a serious breach. A member was intimidated verbally and physically, and that behaviour cannot be condoned or accepted by parlament ... and the speaker must act," Anderton said.
He said he was also concerned about threats he heard Peters make to Banks.
"They were of the kind that can only be interpreted as 'if you do so and so, then I will do so and so to you'."
